wrong_text: The tourism economy generates around £1.4 billion annually and supports roughly 18,000 jobs in the region.
problem: Both figures are stale/wrong. The £1.4 billion value is from 2017; the official Cumbria Tourism STEAM data for 2023 gives £2.304 billion and for 2024 gives £2.373 billion for the Lake District. The 18,000 jobs figure has no traceable authoritative source in current LDNPA or Cumbria Tourism data; Cumbria-wide tourism employment is ~74,000. Source: Cumbria Tourism STEAM 2023/2024 (cumbriatourism.org/resources/research).
correction: The tourism economy generates around £2.3 billion annually and supports tens of thousands of jobs across the region.

problem: The 4-mark practice question mark scheme and the conclusion repeat the same stale £1.4 billion figure. Current STEAM figures (2023/2024) are £2.3–2.4 billion. A student citing £1.4bn in an exam would not be penalised for using a textbook figure, but the lesson itself should carry current data. Source: Cumbria Tourism STEAM 2024.

wrong_text: Thirlmere (Manchester since 1894) and Haweswater (raised 1930s, serves the North West).
problem: Thirlmere's attribution to Manchester is accurate (opened 13 Oct 1894). However, Haweswater also supplies Greater Manchester and Lancashire via the Haweswater Aqueduct (2.5 million customers in Greater Manchester and Lancashire), not just 'the North West' generically. This is not wrong, just imprecise — flagged LOW. More important: the answer implies Haweswater was 'raised 1930s'; the dam was completed 1935 and the valley flooded through the late 1930s, so '1930s' is correct.
correction: Thirlmere (Manchester since 1894) and Haweswater (raised 1930s, supplies Greater Manchester and Lancashire).
